resale_co.name: Certificate of Construction Records Clearance (CRC), described on the Township site as a Municipal Code Compliance Inspection
resale_co.issued_by: Clinton Township Construction Code Enforcement (Building Department)
resale_co.lead_time: The Township processes requests made more than 10 business days ahead within 10 business days; later requests cost more and timing is not guaranteed
resale_co.valid_for: Six months from the date of issuance, provided no change in occupancy has occurred
requirements: Records inspection for open construction permits and pending, open, unabated violations
All building permits must be closed out (final inspections and prior approvals obtained) and violations cured before the certificate is issued
Bring the completed application and fee to the Building Department to schedule

fees.label: Construction Records Clearance, more than 10 business days before closing
Construction Records Clearance, 10 business days or less before closing
Updated certificate (update of a prior records inspection within six months)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Complete the Construction Records Clearance Application and bring it with the fee to the Building Department, 1225 Route 31 South, Building D, 1st Floor, Lebanon. Choose call-to-pick-up or email delivery on the form.
resale_co.contact_title: Technical Assistant (Construction Official: Tom Petto, ext. 256, tpetto@clintontwpnj.org)

evidence.quote: Whenever a house, apartment, or any other structure is rented or sold, The Clinton Township Code section 158-8 A requires the current owner to obtain a Municipal Code Compliance Inspection.
You must complete the following form and bring it to the Building Department with the fee to schedule an inspection.
All building permits must be closed out before a certificate can be issued.
A CRC shall be required prior to the conveyance of any residential building, or individual residential unit within a building.
For requests made more than 10 business days prior to the change in occupancy, it being acknowledged the Township shall process an application for a CRC within 10 business days
Validity. A CRC shall be valid for a period of six months from the date of its issuance, provided no change in occupancy has occurred during said six months.

resale_co.notes: Township Code 155-8C (amended 12-9-2015 by Ord. No. 1079-15) requires a CRC before any residential conveyance, with exemptions such as deed corrections, transfers between spouses or between parent and child, estate distributions, refinancing and any transfer that does not change occupancy. A buyer may agree in writing to take responsibility for the CRC before occupying. The construction page cites 'section 158-8 A', but the CRC is actually in Code 155-8C. The page calls it a Municipal Code Compliance Inspection and says to bring the form in 'to schedule an inspection', while the ordinance describes a records inspection; ask whether a site visit happens. Contacts (Terri Howell, Tom Petto) come from the department page contact block, which loads by script. The packs.json ecode link (CL0749) is the Town of Clinton's code; Clinton Township's code is ecode360.com/CL1920.

requirements: Smoke alarm on each level of the home and outside each separate sleeping area
Battery-only smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed battery units; hardwired alarms from original construction may not be replaced with battery alarms
Carbon monoxide alarm in the immediate vicinity of the sleeping areas (where there is a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage)
Secondary power source identification label, only if the home has a secondary power source (added by P.L.2025, c.19)

fire_cert.notes: Clinton Township enforces the fire code locally through its Bureau of Fire Safety (LEA code M), which also serves Lebanon Borough. Code 133-10 sets $50 / $90 / $161 plus a $50 reinspection or no-show fee, matching the 2025-03-26 application. The application already reflects P.L.2025, c.19: it drops the portable fire extinguisher and adds the secondary power source identification label. Code 133-10 still names the certificate as including a portable fire extinguisher, but the newer form controls in practice. Fire Marshal contact details (Frank Ur, ext. 254, firemarshal@clintontwpnj.org) come from the Fire Safety page contact block, which loads by script; the state directory lists fireinspector2@clintontwpnj.org.
